newsitem.title: INDIA: Four injured in Indian Kashmir grenade attack.
newsitem.headline: Four injured in Indian Kashmir grenade attack.

text.p: At least four people were injured on Sunday in a grenade attack in a busy marketplace in troubled Kashmir's biggest city, police said.

They said four civilians were injured when suspected separatist guerrillas lobbed a grenade at a security patrol in the crowded Amira Kadal market in the heart of Srinagar, the summer capital of India's Jammu and Kashmir state. The grenade missed the patrol and exploded on the road.
Suspected separatist guerrillas hurled another grenade at a paramilitary patrol at Nowhatta, a downtown locality of Srinagar which exploded without any loss of life, police said.
Earlier on Sunday nine policemen were wounded when a device tied to the body of a slain Moslem militant exploded by accident, police said.
The latest violence in the disputed Himalayan territory coincided with talks between Indian and Pakistani diplomats in New Delhi, the first such formal discussions for three years.
On Saturday, a car bomb blew up in a crowded bus station in Jammu, the state's winter capital, killing 16 people and wounding about 70, police and hospital doctors said.
